_comment: P3G.2 (#22) PR-blocking gate baseline. pass_rate is (passed / (passed + failed)) among NON-xfail cases for the category, from a clean `pytest evals/ -m "not integration"` run -- see evals/conftest.py's pytest_sessionfinish hook and evals/runner/gate.py. Regenerate by running the suite and updating a category's pass_rate deliberately (in its own commit, with a reason) whenever an intentional, reviewed change lowers it -- never to silence an unexplained regression.

citation_present._note: #114 (this fix moves the total from 3/12 to 4/12): re-investigated #109's flagged statin-ck-myopathy-question chart-data-only pattern (previously #106: 4/4 draws never attempted a guideline citation) at a much larger live sample -- 3 separate batches (10 + 10 + 5 = 25 draws total, production LlamaServerClient, evals.runner.pipeline.run_case, no replay). Found 23/25 draws (92%) reach verified with a real, verbatim statin-monitoring guideline_chunk DocumentCitation -- the small-sample chart-data-only finding does not reproduce at scale. NO prompting or extraction-code change was made: the 2 non-passing draws (both in the first batch) could not be root-caused -- a diagnostic-script mistake (piping through `tail -80` inside a backgrounded shell command) destroyed their individual detail before they could be inspected, so per this issue's own conservative instruction, no fix was invented for a mechanism that was never actually reproduced and inspected. Most likely explanation: other work already merged in this sequence (#105's guideline_excerpts-into-planner fix, #108's duplicate-claim judge fix) improved this case as a side effect without a re-measurement since #106/#109's smaller samples -- the same stale-small-sample pattern #113/#116 also found elsewhere. statin-ck-myopathy-question's xfail marker was removed; the first live re-record attempt landed on verified, consistent with the 92% typical outcome, not cherry-picked. See docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md, 'Issue #114 findings', for the full trace. #115 (does not change pass_rate or the 3/12 total -- both cases remain honestly xfail): root-caused the SourceRef misattribution #109 flagged for dual-antiplatelet-question/hypertension-lifestyle-followup-question. Live re-verification (production LlamaServerClient, run_case, temperature=0 -- every draw byte-identical, 6+ draws for dual-antiplatelet, 3+ for hypertension) found genuine FABRICATION, not a #85-style recoverable misrouted-ref shape: both questions state the relevant chart fact directly in the question text (medications / blood pressure + lifestyle plan), so the planner never dispatches get_medications/get_vitals at all -- the extractor then invents a syntactically well-formed but entirely fabricated SourceRef (a real call_id paired with a field name that appears in NO real tool-result catalog entry) to back the claim anyway, alongside a genuinely VALID, verbatim guideline_chunk DocumentCitation on some claims (both cases DO cite their guideline chunk correctly -- that half of #109's finding holds). Per this issue's own conservative instruction, no coercion fix was implemented: there is no reconstructable structure to safely recover from (unlike #85's <doc_id>#<section> shape), and even a narrow fix for the one recoverable-looking duplicate-ref pattern would not flip either case to verified (other, unrelated claims in the same answer are separately and independently fabricated with no valid citation to fall back on). check_claim's existing fail-closed AND-aggregation already handles this correctly; a hermetic regression test (test_verification_documents.py) now locks in this exact shape. The upstream, out-of-scope root cause (the planner never dispatching a confirming tool call for a chart fact the question already states, so no real citable record exists at all) is filed as issue #123 for the maintainer. See docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md, 'Issue #115 findings', for the full trace. #116 (this fix supersedes the #108 note below): re-verified warfarin-antibiotic-question and metformin-renal-monitoring-question live (production LlamaServerClient, evals.runner.pipeline.run_case, no replay, 10 fresh draws each) -- the ORIGINAL chart-data-only xfail rationale for both is stale (does not reproduce), but only warfarin-antibiotic-question actually moves off xfail: it verified 10/10 with two real, verbatim guideline_chunk DocumentCitations passing both provenance AND semantic support every time. metformin-renal-monitoring-question's verdict also reaches verified 10/10, but for the WRONG reason -- the claim extractor never attaches a real DocumentCitation for the guideline quote; instead it duplicates an unrelated, trivially-valid chart-data SourceRef several times per guideline-derived claim, which satisfies check_claim's citation-validity AND-aggregation without ever citing the guideline. guideline_citation_present correctly fails 10/10, so the case remains honestly xfail with a rationale describing this newly-observed extraction-misattribution mechanism (also correcting issue #109's own spike finding for this case). A larger (10-draw) live sample was also taken of statin-liver-monitoring-question's chart-data-only behavior specifically (flagged inconclusive by #109 at n=3): 0/13 combined draws reproduced a chart-data-only outcome, ruling that pattern out as a small-sample artifact -- but the case still did not reach verified in any of the 10 new draws (a different, unrelated mechanism), so it remains honestly xfail too. pass_rate is 1.0 because CategoryStats.pass_rate is computed over non-xfail cases only (3 passed / 0 failed here) -- honest gate-ON total is now 3/12, up from the previous 2/12 (see docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md, 'Issue #116 follow-up'). #108's prior note, for history: app.semantic_support's duplicate-claim judge inconsistency (two claims restating one guideline-backed fact, both citing the IDENTICAL DocumentCitation, judged with two independent -- and sometimes disagreeing -- LLM calls) was fixed by grouping DocumentCitation results by exact evidence identity and judging each identity once. Live re-verification: a1c-target-question 7/8 draws verified, lithium-nsaid-question 8/8 draws verified; both cases' xfail markers were removed and fresh verified recordings committed, moving the total from 0/12 to 2/12 at that time. #100's prior note, for history: the committed 5/12 baseline's 5 non-xfail cases (bp-stage2-question, a1c-target-question, dual-antiplatelet-question, hypertension-lifestyle-followup-question, lithium-nsaid-question) each reflected one STABLE, frozen recording from an earlier draw that was never re-checked against a fresh live draw; re-running all 5 live found every one of them failed to reliably reproduce verified at that time (1/42 live draws). bp-stage2-question, dual-antiplatelet-question, and hypertension-lifestyle-followup-question remain xfail today for reasons unrelated to #108/#116 (see docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md). #113 (this fix does not change pass_rate or the 3/12 total): re-investigated #109's flagged 0.62-below-floor finding for lipid-panel-ldl-question and found it does not reproduce reliably -- 10 fresh live rerank draws of the same (query, chunk) pair scored 0.85 in 9/10 and 0.62 in 1/10, so the floor (0.75, issue #99) is not a systematic miss for this topic. No threshold change was made: #99's own calibration data already has planted distractors scoring 0.65, above the 0.62 outlier, so any floor low enough to reliably admit it would also reopen distractor leakage. Separately, 10 fresh live draws (bypassing the floor entirely, mirroring #109/#115/#116's method) found the case still reaches only partially_verified, 10/10 -- a newly-discovered, distinct SourceRef-misrouting variant (the model puts the same doc_id in both tool_call_id and record_id, which issue #85's existing coercion does not reconstruct), filed separately as issue #125 rather than fixed here. lipid-panel-ldl-question's xfail rationale was rewritten to describe this precisely (the prior #58-era 'never quotes the guideline' reasoning was stale) with a fresh recording committed. See docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md, 'Issue #113 findings', for the full trace. #125 (this fix does not change pass_rate or the 4/12 total): fixed the doc_id-doubled SourceRef-misrouting variant #113 found -- _coerce_misrouted_guideline_refs (app/extraction.py) now also recognizes tool_call_id==record_id==doc_id (no section slug) and reconstructs the real chunk id whenever it identifies exactly one retrieved chunk's doc_id unambiguously (an adversarial regression test locks in that an ambiguous multi-chunk doc_id collision is never coerced). Live re-verification (18 fresh draws total, production LlamaServerClient, evals.runner.pipeline.run_case, no replay) confirms the fix: 18/18 draws now produce a real, verbatim guideline_chunk DocumentCitation that passes provenance re-validation (CitationStatus.VALID) -- the #125 defect no longer reproduces. But the case still does not reach verified: a separate, newly-discovered defect in app.semantic_support's post-provenance judge gate (the claim asserting 'considered high' is judged in isolation, without the sibling claim's actual LDL value, so the judge -- reasonably, given only what it's shown -- downgrades it to NOT_SEMANTICALLY_SUPPORTED 8/8 times) blocks it instead, filed separately as issue #128 (out of #125's own scope). lipid-panel-ldl-question's xfail rationale was rewritten again to describe this precisely, with a fresh recording committed; it remains honestly xfail. See docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md, 'Issue #125 findings', for the full trace. #118 (this fix does not change pass_rate or the 4/12 total): re-investigated #116's own metformin-renal-monitoring-question finding above ('the claim extractor never attaches a real DocumentCitation for the guideline quote') and found IT does not reproduce either -- 10 fresh live draws (production LlamaServerClient, evals.runner.pipeline.run_case, no replay, this time with the issue #47/#81 semantic-support gate correctly applied, which the #116 measurement omitted) show the extractor reliably attaching a real, verbatim, semantically-supported guideline_chunk DocumentCitation to the claims that need one, 10/10 -- guideline_citation_present now PASSES 10/10 for this case. The case still does not reach verified, though, for a THIRD, distinct mechanism: a 4th, over-generalized claim ('the exact frequency... should be determined based on individual health status') cites a real guideline passage that does not actually support that specific generalization, and the semantic-support judge correctly downgrades it to NOT_SEMANTICALLY_SUPPORTED, 10/10 draws -- this looks like the gate working as intended, not a defect, so no fix was applied for it. #118's own hypothesis (an irrelevant, duplicated SourceRef standing in for a missing guideline citation, with check_claim needing a relevance check on ordinary SourceRefs to catch it) is filed as a still-open, currently-unexercised design question in issue #130 rather than fixed here, since no live-reproducible case currently needs it. A characterization test (services/copilot-agent/tests/test_verification.py::test_source_ref_relevance_is_not_checked_structural_validity_only) documents the accepted gap. metformin-renal-monitoring-question's xfail rationale was rewritten again to describe this precisely, with a fresh recording committed; it remains honestly xfail (verdict, not guideline_citation_present, is now the blocking assertion). See docs/MODEL_AND_HARDWARE_SELECTION.md, 'Issue #118 follow-up', for the full trace. #111/#128 (this fix moves the total from 4/12 to 6/12): both issues traced to the same root cause -- app.semantic_support.judge_support/apply_semantic_support only ever received one claim's isolated text plus one citation's quote, with no visibility into (a) that SAME claim's OTHER citations (#111: bp-stage2-question's guideline citation judged without the sibling chart-data SourceRef establishing 148/94 mmHg, on the SAME claim) or (b) SIBLING claims in the same answer (#128: lipid-panel-ldl-question's 'considered high' claim judged without the separate claim's '172 mg/dL' SourceRef value). Fix: apply_semantic_support now gathers every already-deterministically-verified SourceRef fact -- the claim's own, plus any sibling claim's whose citations are ALL SourceRefs and which has already fully passed -- and hands it to the judge as an additional ESTABLISHED FACTS block, so a category/threshold guideline quote can be judged against the specific value it categorizes even when the quote itself never restates that value. Safety invariant (explicit in code, tested): only ground truth already confirmed by deterministic re-validation (CitationStatus.VALID SourceRefs) is ever surfaced; a sibling claim that failed provenance, or whose own fact still depends on an unjudged DocumentCitation, is excluded -- never a fabricated or merely-asserted fact. Live re-verification (production LlamaServerClient, evals.runner.pipeline.run_case, no replay): bp-stage2-question 25/25 verified across two independent multi-draw sessions, plus 4/4 more via evals/runner/record.py itself; lipid-panel-ldl-question 25/25 verified plus 4/4 more via record.py. (Two earlier record.py invocations from a misconfigured investigation container transiently showed partially_verified -- root-caused to that container's directory layout not matching runner/record.py's assumed evals/-sibling-to-services/copilot-agent/ structure, which silently fell back to a STALE, pre-fix site-packages copy of app/semantic_support.py; not a defect in the fix itself, confirmed once the container mount layout was corrected.) statin-liver-monitoring-question (bonus candidate per the prior session's assessment) was spot-checked (6 draws) and did NOT flip -- it remains a genuine judge-correct rejection (the guideline quote says routine monitoring is usually NOT needed for an asymptomatic patient, while the claim asserts it IS needed -- a real direction mismatch, unrelated to context-scoping), so it is left alone. Both bp-stage2-question's and lipid-panel-ldl-question's xfail markers were removed with fresh verified recordings committed. See the PR description for issues #111/#128 for the full trace.
